findings.problem: load_packets fuses file I/O (fs::read_to_string), logging (println), parsing, and domain construction into a single function, violating Data/Calculations/Actions architecture. The shell should handle I/O and pass DTOs to pure parsing logic.
findings.failure_mode: Cannot unit-test the parsing and construction logic without real files; cannot swap storage backends; logging is embedded in domain path and cannot be disabled or redirected.
findings.fix: Split into a shell function that reads bytes and a pure parse_records function that takes &[str] and returns Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError>. Move println to the shell boundary.

findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics when the file is missing, unreadable, or not valid UTF-8.
findings.failure_mode: Complete process crash on absent or malformed input file instead of returning a typed I/O error that callers can handle gracefully.
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, IoError> (or a domain error enum) and propagate the error with ? instead of unwrap.

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics when the value field is not a valid integer.
findings.failure_mode: Process crash on malformed CSV data instead of returning a typed ParseError that distinguishes invalid format from valid-but-out-of-range values.
findings.fix: Use .parse::<u16>().map_err(|e| ParseError::Invalid)? or .parse::<u32>().map_err(|_| ParseError::Invalid)? with a domain-typed error return.

findings.problem: as u16 silently truncates a u32 parse result. Values above 65535 wrap to a small number without error.
findings.failure_mode: Invalid domain state: a value like 70000 parses successfully and silently becomes 4464, corrupting data without any caller awareness.
findings.fix: Use u16::try_from(parsed_u32).map_err(|_| ParseError::Overflow)? or parse directly as u16 with .parse::<u16>().map_err(...). This makes out-of-range a typed error, not silent truncation.

findings.problem: parts[0] and parts[1] use index access without bounds checking. Malformed lines with fewer than 2 comma-separated fields will panic at runtime.
findings.failure_mode: Runtime panic (index out of bounds) on malformed input instead of a typed error. The bounds check is hidden inside the index operator, making it unreachable through error handling.
findings.fix: Use line.split_once(',').ok_or(ParseError::Invalid)? to get (name_str, value_str) safely, avoiding Vec allocation and index bounds entirely. For two-field records, split_once is the correct pattern per hardening checklist.

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) embeds side-effect I/O inside the data-parsing map closure, violating the Calculations layer which must be pure and deterministic.
findings.failure_mode: Side-effectful code inside iterator pipeline is not observable or testable; output depends on external console state; makes the function non-deterministic from a testing perspective.
findings.fix: Remove println from the parse path. If logging is needed, return a result that the shell layer can log, or use a pure callback/writer abstraction injected by the shell.

findings.problem: Raw String primitives flow through the entire pipeline without a parse boundary. The name field is a raw String with no invariants, and CSV strings are parsed inline without a dedicated parse function that converts external input into trusted domain values.
findings.failure_mode: Callers can construct Record with any String value (empty, whitespace, embedded commas), making illegal states representable at the type level. No smart constructor enforces domain invariants.
findings.fix: Introduce a RecordName newtype with a smart constructor that validates non-empty and invariant properties. Add a dedicated parse_record function that takes raw CSV lines and returns Result<Record, ParseError>, enforcing all invariants at the parse boundary.

findings.problem: Record uses pub name: String, a raw string field with no type-level constraints. The name could be empty, contain invalid characters, or violate domain rules.
findings.failure_mode: Invalid record names are representable at the type level; any caller can create a Record with an empty or malformed name string.
findings.fix: Replace String with a RecordName newtype that has a private constructor and validates on creation. Encode name invariants in the type system so invalid names cannot be constructed.

findings.problem: Vec::with_capacity equivalent via collect() from split has no domain cap on line count and no try_reserve. Every line allocates a new Vec<String> with trim + to_string allocations.
findings.failure_mode: Unbounded allocation per line and per record; a large file causes unbounded heap growth with no cap. Each line's intermediate Vec and String allocations are unbounded and unmeasured.
findings.fix: Validate a domain cap/max rows before iteration. Use Vec::new() with try_reserve(max_lines).map_err(|_| AllocationError)? before the collect loop. For single-line parsing, replace the Vec allocation entirely with split_once as noted above.

findings.problem: Function allocates a Vec per line (split + trim + to_string + collect), then a Vec for the final result. No benchmark, baseline measurement, profiler data, or allocation evidence exists to justify the approach.
findings.failure_mode: Performance characteristics are unknown; intermediate allocations could be eliminated with streaming or split_once; allocation pattern may be unacceptable in mission-critical paths per Holzman allocation discipline.
findings.fix: Add a benchmark comparing the current approach vs. split_once + &str-based parsing. Report ops/sec or items/sec with workload details. If allocation is in a hot path, use try_reserve and consider returning &str-backed records or a zero-copy design.

findings.problem: No cargo fmt, cargo check, cargo clippy, cargo test, or benchmark commands were executed. No evidence that the code compiles, passes lint gates, or has correct behavior.
findings.failure_mode: The code may not even compile; clippy warnings (unwrap_used, indexing_slicing, arithmetic_side_effects) are unverified; no test coverage evidence exists.
findings.fix: Run cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy with strict gates, cargo test, and document results. Add behavior tests covering valid input, malformed CSV, missing file, overflow, and empty input.

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for the stated or implied performance of load_packets
no profiler evidence for allocation patterns (per-line Vec/String allocation)
no allocation budget or try_reserve evidence for bounded allocation
no second-ring evidence (compiler IR, assembly) for any performance claim
no command evidence: cargo fmt, cargo clippy, cargo check, cargo test have not been run
no behavior tests exist for error paths (missing file, malformed CSV, overflow)
residual_risk: This crate has 11 findings (8 BLOCKER, 3 MAJOR). All absolute laws are violated: no production unwrap allowed but two are present; no hidden I/O allowed but file I/O and println are in the parse path; no lossy casts allowed but as u16 truncates silently; no unchecked indexing allowed but parts[0] and parts[1] lack bounds guards. The function must be split into shell and pure parsing layers, all unwrap/expect/panic surfaces must be replaced with typed errors, the lossy as u16 cast must become try_from, indexing must become split_once, and a RecordName newtype must enforce name invariants. No delivery is possible until all BLOCKER findings are resolved.
